name: Vanya and Computer Game
description: Vanya and his friend Vova play a computer game where they need to destroy n monsters to pass a level. Vanya's character performs attack with frequency x hits per second and Vova's character performs attack with frequency y hits per second. Each character spends fixed time to raise a weapon and then he hits (the time to raise the weapon is 1 / x seconds for the first character and 1 / y seconds for the second one). The i -th monster dies after he receives a i hits. Vanya and Vova wonder who makes the last hit on each monster. If Vanya and Vova make the last hit at the same time, we assume that both of them have made the last hit.
input_specification: The first line contains three integers n , x , y ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 , 1 ≤ x , y ≤ 10 6 ) — the number of monsters, the frequency of Vanya's and Vova's attack, correspondingly. Next n lines contain integers a i ( 1 ≤ a i ≤ 10 9 ) — the number of hits needed do destroy the i -th monster.
output_specification: Print n lines. In the i -th line print word " Vanya ", if the last hit on the i -th monster was performed by Vanya, " Vova ", if Vova performed the last hit, or " Both ", if both boys performed it at the same time.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 492D — Vanya and Computer Game [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
